answer: Reputation that decays is a ledge no fake identity can stand on for long. In an agent economy, each identity's trust score fades steadily unless it keeps doing verifiable, useful work, so a sybil army must pay the full cost of good behavior for every fake, forever. One burst of fake activity cannot echo into lasting influence, and an attacker who stops paying that upkeep slides back toward zero before reaching the zenith of high-trust privileges like large escrow or jury seats. Maintaining thousands of decaying identities costs more than any fraud they could extract.
